biography: Steve Watkins, a product of the gritty British karting scene, began his racing journey at the tender age of eight. His father, a former mechanic, instilled in him a deep understanding of race car engineering from a young age. He progressed quickly through the ranks, winning several national karting championships. Watkins's break came in the Formula Ford series, where he secured a stunning last-lap victory at Brands Hatch, showcasing his remarkable overtaking prowess. This victory catapulted him into the MCR S2000 team. Now at 34, Watkins is considered to be at his peak, meticulously analysing every aspect of his performance and the car's setup. He consistently scores podium finishes but is hungry for his first championship title, relentlessly pursuing perfection.
drivingStyle: Watkins is a calculating and precise driver, known for his exceptional car control and strategic race management. He doesn't often take unnecessary risks early in a race, preferring to conserve his tires and exploit opportunities as they arise. In qualifying, he is a master of stringing together the perfect lap, often extracting the maximum potential from his car. Under pressure, Watkins remains remarkably calm, able to make quick decisions and execute precise maneuvers even in the most challenging conditions. He's a late-braking specialist, often surprising opponents with audacious overtakes.

rivalries.reason: Rossi and Watkins have a long-standing rivalry stemming from a controversial incident at Silverstone where Rossi accused Watkins of overly aggressive defending, costing him valuable championship points.
Dubois and Watkins often clash on track, particularly in wet conditions. Dubois believes Watkins benefits unfairly from his team's superior wet weather setup.
Tanaka's aggressive and unpredictable driving style often puts him at odds with Watkins' more calculated approach, leading to frequent on-track altercations.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky socks on race day, regardless of the weather.
Spends at least 30 minutes meditating before each race to clear his mind and focus.
Carries a small, worn-out teddy bear in his helmet bag, a childhood keepsake his father gave him.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't just about speed; it's about understanding the chess game unfolding at 200 miles per hour."
careerHighlight: Winning the Silverstone 24 Hours in 2021 with MCR, battling through torrential rain and numerous mechanical issues to secure a historic victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the 2022 championship decider at Monza due to a sudden tire failure, costing him the title.
